title: One token is about four characters
summary: The rule of thumb behind chatbot prices: one token is about four characters of English, or three quarters of a word.

beats.say: The unit most chatbot prices use is about four characters long.
Models do not read words. They read chunks called tokens.
OpenAI and Google both publish the same rule of thumb.
beats.cap: Same rule from OpenAI and Google

beats.say: One token is about four characters of English.
That is about three quarters of a word.
So one hundred tokens come to about seventy five words.
OpenAI's own example: fifteen hundred words are about two thousand forty eight tokens.
Other languages can need more tokens per character.
beats.cap: Not every language costs the same

beats.say: OpenAI's example: ten Spanish characters took five tokens.
The same token budget can buy fewer words in some languages.

claims.note: OpenAI help: 100 tokens is about 75 words
OpenAI help: 1,500 words is about 2,048 tokens
OpenAI help: 1,500 words is about 2,048 tokens

facts.claim: OpenAI's help page says one token is about 4 characters of English text, about 3/4 of a word
facts.note: OpenAI help, what are tokens: 1 token ~= 4 chars in English; 1 token ~= 3/4 words; 100 tokens ~= 75 words

facts.claim: OpenAI's help page gives 1,500 words as about 2,048 tokens
facts.note: OpenAI help: 1-2 sentences ~= 30 tokens, 1 paragraph ~= 100 tokens, 1,500 words ~= 2,048 tokens

facts.claim: OpenAI's help page says the Spanish phrase 'Cómo estás' is 5 tokens for 10 characters and that other languages can cost more
facts.note: OpenAI help: token-to-character ratios are higher for many other languages; example 'Cómo estás' = 5 tokens, 10 characters

facts.claim: Google's Gemini documentation says a token is equivalent to about 4 characters, and 100 tokens is roughly 60 to 80 English words
facts.note: Gemini API docs, Understand and count tokens: a token is equivalent to about 4 characters; 100 tokens is about 60-80 English words
